title: Owens Field
description: Large concrete park with bowls, ledges, and a street section. Well-maintained and popular with locals.
tips: Best sessions are late at night, there are plenty of people and it's well lit.
Watch your stuff late at night, little kids tend to steal stuff.
The bowls are intense, be confident before dropping in.
After the park gate closes, you can park in the tennis lot and walk over.

title: Irmo Skate Park
description: Concrete park in Rawls Creek with a flow bowl, quarter pipes, and street features. Hosts Nike SB events.
tips: Mornings are the best time to have the bowl to yourself.
The flat rail gets slick after rain, give it a day to dry.
Parking is free and right next to the park.
Bring water, there's no shade over the street section.

title: Russell House
description: Long marble banks alongside the university buildings. Great for carving and manual lines.
tips: Weekend mornings are dead, best time to skate.
Don't skate during football game days, way too crowded.
Keep an eye out for campus security, they'll ask you to leave during events.
Combine with a session at Close Hipp since they're a few blocks apart.

title: Close Hipp
description: Smoothest concrete in the city in the underground parking lot. Lots of manual pads.
location: Harden St & Devine St, Columbia, SC
tips: Go after 6pm or on weekends when the garage is mostly empty.
Watch for cars coming around the corners, they can't see you well.
It's good for skating after it rains, but some oil pots can be slick.
Bring water, it stays really hot down there.

title: T-Coop Fountain
description: Massive 8-stair gap with rough landing. Not for the faint of heart.
tips: Bring a broom, the run-up is covered in debris.
Landing is rough, softer wheels or bigger wheels help.
Skate it early morning to avoid traffic on Bull St.
Not a solo spot, always bring a friend.

title: Gambrell
description: Large variety of stair sets, large area of flatground.
tips: Great warm-up spot before heading to Owens Field.
The biggest stair set is on the far side, scope it first.
Plenty of parking.
Lights stay on late, night sessions are solid.

title: Bluetile Skate Shop
description: Columbia's original core skate shop. Riders on the team, deep deck selection, and genuine community energy.

title: Salty's Board Shop
description: Great shop for buying complete, good quality cruiser boards. Also a great shop to buy pads.

title: Grindhouse Skate Shop
description: A small business recently established skate shop ran by locals. Has a large supply of used clothes and boards.

title: Ollie
description: The foundation of all skateboarding. Pop the tail, slide your front foot up, and level the board in the air.
mistakes: Slamming the tail in the ground, it's more like dribbling a basketball, not stomping the tail.
Jumping too early before the tail hits the ground.
Front foot not dragging high enough, resulting in a rocketed ollie.
Landing with feet too close together, aim for shoulder-width.
steps: Place the ball of your foot in the middle of the tail, with your weight mostly on the front foot. Front foot sits behind the front bolts.
Bend your knees and jump, snapping the tail down hard against the ground at the end of it.
As the tail hits, drag your front foot up toward the nose, leveling the board.
Suck your knees up to your chest like Spider-Man to give the board room to rise beneath you.
Land with both feet over the bolts and absorb the impact by bending your knees.

title: Kickflip
description: Ollie with a flick off the heel-side toe to spin the board 360 degrees on its long axis. The first real milestone.
mistakes: Kicking down instead of out, which sends the board into the ground.
Flicking too early before the pop is complete.
Keeping your back foot on the board, it has to get out of the way.
Not jumping high enough, the board needs room to flip.
steps: Set up like an ollie, but with your front foot angled slightly toward the heel edge and closer to the front bolts.
Pop the tail, wait a moment, then flick your front foot outward off the heel-side edge of the nose.
Pull your back foot up and away so the board has room to rotate.
Watch the board spin and catch it with both feet as it comes around.
Land with your feet over the bolts and roll away.

title: Heelflip
description: Like a kickflip but the board flips toe-side. Flick off the heel edge with your front foot going outward.
mistakes: Flicking straight down instead of out off the toe-side edge.
Front foot placed too far toward the toe edge before popping.
Popping too late and the front foot flicks into the ground.
Ensure your back foot is on the balls of your feet, near the heelside of the tail.
steps: Set up like an ollie with your front foot's toe hanging slightly off the toe-side edge.
Pop the tail and flick your front foot outward, using your heel to catch the edge.
Keep your back foot up and away from the board as it flips.
Catch the board with both feet when it completes the rotation.
Absorb the landing with your knees and roll away.

title: 50-50 Grind
description: Lock both trucks onto a ledge or rail and slide. The entry-level grind, learn this before any other.
mistakes: Approaching too parallel to the ledge, come in at a slight angle.
Leaning too far forward or backward on the ledge and slipping out.
Not committing to the ollie and catching the ledge with your wheels.
Forgetting to pop off at the end and just rolling off the edge.
steps: Approach the ledge or rail at a slight angle, roughly 30 degrees.
Pop a small ollie and aim to land both trucks on top of the obstacle.
Keep your weight centered and your knees slightly bent to balance.
Slide until you're ready to come off.
Pop a small ollie off the end or just roll off the side.

title: Nose Grind
description: Balance the front truck only on the obstacle with the tail kicked up. Requires precise weight distribution.
mistakes: Shifting your weight too far forward and falling over the ledge.
Not keeping your back foot ready to catch the tail on the way out.
Approaching too straight on, which makes locking in harder.
Looking down at your feet instead of ahead at the end of the ledge.
steps: Approach the ledge at a slight angle with your weight centered.
Pop an ollie and aim your front truck only onto the ledge.
Keep your back foot hovering over the tail and your front knee bent.
Hold your weight directly over the front truck to stay balanced.
When you're ready, shift your weight back and pop off the ledge.

title: Tre Flip
description: Pop a kickflip while scooping the tail to spin the board 360 degrees backside. Also called a 360 flip.
mistakes: Scooping the tail without popping, which kills the height.
Flicking the front foot too hard and the board over-rotates the flip.
Not scooping hard enough with the back foot, so the spin doesn't happen.
Jumping straight up instead of slightly forward, the board moves.
steps: Set up with your back foot on the tail and your front foot toward the front bolts, toes angled slightly heel-side.
Ensure that your weight is so far back on the board that if you shifted any further back, you'd enter a manual.
Pop the tail hard and scoop it backside with your back foot to start the 360 rotation.
As the board pops, flick your front foot off the heel-side edge to start the flip.
Keep your knees high and watch the board rotate and flip beneath you.
Catch the board with both feet and absorb the landing.
